Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of three line segments. Find the value of
${\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$

${\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$

feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [1,3],$ the line segment for $x\in [3,5],$ and the line segment for $x\in [5,6].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{5}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3+1)\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =lw \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [5,6].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4)\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =4+2+\frac{5}{2} \\  & =\frac{17}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
